quality_issues.detail: Annual real GDP levels span rebasing vintages; do not calculate a long-run real-level CAGR without linking consistent bases. Use published growth rates.
Revenue and expenditure are fiscal-year cumulative; June is the full fiscal year. Do not sum cumulative monthly values. Calendar-year GDP is not a fiscal-year GDP denominator.
Trade CIF imports and FOB exports differ from BPM6 goods measures. Oil re-export revisions limit interpretation of export growth as domestic production.
Expanded monetary survey includes microfinance and SACCOs. Keep separate from standard survey; FX valuation affects foreign-currency credit.
End-period FX download ends at an incomplete August 2011 row; retained raw but excluded from normalized analysis.
Annual GDP file does not explicitly state units/base in its header; KES million inferred from CBK quarterly/BOP context. Confirm metadata before publication.

publication_note: GDP level-derived contributions are provisional. See source-vintage warnings.

current_affairs.scope: Selected attributable institutional, business and household views. This is not a representative social-media sentiment survey.

items.summary: First-half growth was 5.2%; the full-year forecast is 4.6%. Fiscal slippage and governance constrain investment and job creation. The release reports reserves of about USD14.7 billion and 5.9 months of imports, and interest absorbing about one-third of revenue.
items.caveat: Forecasts are not observed annual growth. Reserve and debt reference periods differ from CBK downloaded series.

items.summary: Treasury principal secretary Chris Kiptoo considered the World Bank's 4.6% forecast too pessimistic and expected at least 5% growth. Reuters reports concerns about fiscal slippage and uncertainty ahead of the 2027 election.
items.caveat: Government and World Bank forecasts reflect different assumptions; neither is a 2026 final outturn.

items.summary: October inflation rounded to 7.3%, with food inflation at 10.2%, transport at 17.1%, and housing/utilities at 3.7%. These three expenditure categories represent 57% of the CPI weight.
items.caveat: Rates by category are not contributions to headline inflation. The CBK table carries two-decimal headline precision of 7.32%.

items.summary: CBK held the policy rate at 8.75%; nine of 11 polled economists expected a hold. CBK projected 5.0% growth and a 3.2% current-account deficit in 2026; weather and fuel costs remain risks.
items.caveat: The current-account figure for 2026 is a forecast, not the annual BPM6 outturn.

items.summary: CEOs reported improving optimism and orders but broadly stable production and employment. Rising purchase costs, limited pricing power and credit-access obstacles constrained firms. Seasonal demand was expected to support the following quarter.
items.caveat: The survey targeted 600 firms; this is not the achieved respondent count. CEO expectations are not representative household opinions or realized production.

items.summary: Respondents expected inflation above 5% but within target over the next three months, citing fuel, transport, weather and geopolitical pressures.
items.caveat: Expectations were gathered before the October inflation release.

items.summary: The accessible article reports Stanbic PMI rising from 51.3 in September to 52.5 in October, with more orders but higher operating costs.
items.caveat: Only the publicly accessible introduction was used. PMI is a diffusion index; 52.5 is not 2.5% GDP growth.

items.summary: 61% described the national economy as bad; health, living costs and unemployment were leading concerns. Reported hardship included going without cash income, medical care or enough food.
items.caveat: Historical public-opinion evidence, not a November 2026 sentiment reading. Do not confuse article publication/crawl date with fieldwork date.

items.summary: The article reports that 66% felt personally worse off than before the 2022 election, 12% better off and 23% unchanged. It describes face-to-face interviews with 2,048 adults across all 47 counties. Unemployment/poverty and high prices/taxes were prominent concerns.
items.caveat: Secondary reporting; the original questionnaire and weighting were not independently verified. Rounded shares total 101%. The comparison is with 2022, not the previous month, and this is not a November sentiment estimate.
